raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #3177

## Problem
transformers loads the tensors a model lists in `_keep_in_fp32_modules` (under fp16) and
`_keep_in_fp32_modules_strict` (under fp16 and bf16) in fp32, because they overflow or lose precision in
half precision. T5/MT5/UMT5/LongT5/SwitchTransformers list their `wo` projection
(huggingface/transformers#20683, added in Dec 2022 for exactly the FlanT5-XL fp16 case), and 17 MoE
model files (DeepSeek-V3, GLM-4.5, ...) list the routing bias `e_score_correction_bias` under both dtypes.

`InferenceEngine._convert_to_dtype` (`deepspeed/inference/engine.py:521-524`) then calls
`self.module.half()` / `self.module.bfloat16()` on the whole model and casts those tensors with everything
else. With `mp_size=1` and no kernel injection (the reporter's call) nothing else in `init_inference`
touches the model, so this cast is the entire difference from Hugging Face.

Impact: silent-wrong-result. Who reaches it / triggered by: anyone calling
`deepspeed.init_inference(model, dtype=torch.float16)` (fp16 is also the config's default `dtype`) or
`dtype=torch.bfloat16` on a transformers model with one of those lists, e.g. the script in #3177. What is
observed: generations that differ from the same model run in transformers, with no warning or error.

Measured here on CPU with `google/flan-t5-base` loaded with `dtype=torch.float16` (transformers 5.17.0,
torch 2.14.0+cpu; the CPU accelerator's fp16 gate was bypassed in the script so the cast path runs), on
the two sentences from the issue, greedy, `max_length=32`:

```
upstream/master:
wo dtype after init_inference: torch.float16
HF: ['Verbal punishment is a form of punishment that is used to punish a child for a crime.', 'I am .']
DS: ['a slap on the head', "I am n't doing it right"]
identical: False

this PR:
wo dtype after init_inference: torch.float32
DS: ['Verbal punishment is a form of punishment that is used to punish a child for a crime.', 'I am .']
identical: True
```

The `.half()` line dates from the 2021 inference release (ed3de0c2), before transformers introduced the
lists, so this is drift rather than a decision. The training side gained `keep_in_fp32_pattern` for the
same lists in #8699 (ZeRO-3); the inference engine was left out.

## Fix
Before casting, collect the fp32 tensors whose full names match the model's lists (reusing
`keep_in_fp32_pattern(module, "auto", dtype)` from #8699, which applies the strict list under bf16 and both
lists under fp16, the way transformers does), cast the module, and put those tensors back. A listed tensor
that arrives in a lower precision is upcast, as transformers' loader and #8699 do. The kept tensors are
the ones transformers already runs with under fp16, and the HF forward passes already cast activations to
the weight dtype for them, so the module ends in the state transformers itself produces. Kernel injection
and AutoTP run after this point and are unchanged.

## Testing
New `tests/unit/inference/test_inference_keep_in_fp32.py`: a toy module with both lists, parametrized over
fp16/bf16 (fp16 skips where the accelerator lacks it), plus a real `T5ForConditionalGeneration` built from
a tiny config under fp16.

Negative control (revert only `deepspeed/inference/engine.py` to `upstream/master`, keep the new test), on
`test_init_inference_keeps_listed_tensors_in_fp32[dtype1]` (bf16, the one this CPU can run):

```
FAILED ...test_init_inference_keeps_listed_tensors_in_fp32[dtype1] - AssertionError
1 failed
```
Restored: `1 passed`. The fp16 cases pass with the fix and fail without it when the fp16 gate is bypassed
locally; on CPU CI they skip and will run on the GPU jobs. `test_inference_config.py`: 9 passed, 1
pre-existing failure (`test_cuda_graph_with_kernel_inject_raises` fails identically on unmodified
`upstream/master` because this CPU has no fp16).

Execution hardware: CPU only (no GPU available to me), torch 2.14.0+cpu. `pre-commit run --files` clean
on both changed files.

Signed-off-by: Udaya Tejas <udayatejas2004@gmail.com>

+# Copyright (c) DeepSpeed Team.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+# DeepSpeed Team
+"""init_inference(dtype=fp16/bf16) keeps the tensors a model names for fp32 in fp32.
+
+transformers loads the tensors a model lists in `_keep_in_fp32_modules` (under fp16) and
+`_keep_in_fp32_modules_strict` (under fp16 and bf16) in fp32, because they overflow or lose precision in
+half precision. Regression test for https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/issues/3177, where
+init_inference cast T5's `wo` projection to fp16 along with the rest of the model.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import deepspeed
+from deepspeed.accelerator import get_accelerator
+
+HIDDEN = 8
+# Distinct in fp32, but fp16 and bf16 round all of them to 8.0.
+EXACT_VALUES = 8.0 + torch.arange(HIDDEN, dtype=torch.float32) * 1e-4
+
+
+class ToyModel(torch.nn.Module):
+    _keep_in_fp32_modules = ["wo"]  # fp16 only, as T5 lists its `wo` projection
+    _keep_in_fp32_modules_strict = ["router_bias"]  # fp16 and bf16, as the MoE models list their routing bias
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.wi = torch.nn.Linear(HIDDEN, HIDDEN, bias=False)
+        self.wo = torch.nn.Linear(HIDDEN, HIDDEN, bias=False)
+        self.register_buffer("router_bias", EXACT_VALUES.clone())
+        self.register_buffer("scale", torch.ones(HIDDEN))
+
+
+def _dtypes(model):
+    return {name: t.dtype for name, t in list(model.named_parameters()) + list(model.named_buffers())}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.inference
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+def test_init_inference_keeps_listed_tensors_in_fp32(dtype):
+    if dtype not in get_accelerator().supported_dtypes():
+        pytest.skip(f"{dtype} not supported by {get_accelerator().device_name()}")
+    model = ToyModel().to(get_accelerator().device_name())
+
+    engine = deepspeed.init_inference(model, dtype=dtype)
+
+    dtypes = _dtypes(engine.module)
+    assert dtypes["wi.weight"] == dtype
+    assert dtypes["scale"] == dtype
+    assert dtypes["router_bias"] == torch.float32
+    # Kept as loaded, not rounded through half precision and cast back.
+    assert torch.equal(engine.module.router_bias.cpu(), EXACT_VALUES)
+    # `_keep_in_fp32_modules` applies under fp16 only, the way transformers applies it.
+    assert dtypes["wo.weight"] == (torch.float32 if dtype == torch.float16 else dtype)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.inference
+@pytest.mark.skipif(torch.float16 not in get_accelerator().supported_dtypes(), reason="fp16 not supported")
+def test_init_inference_fp16_keeps_t5_wo_in_fp32():
+    from transformers import T5Config, T5ForConditionalGeneration
+
+    config = T5Config(vocab_size=64,
+                      d_model=32,
+                      d_kv=8,
+                      d_ff=64,
+                      num_layers=1,
+                      num_decoder_layers=1,
+                      num_heads=2,
+                      decoder_start_token_id=0)
+    model = T5ForConditionalGeneration(config).to(get_accelerator().device_name())
+
+    engine = deepspeed.init_inference(model, dtype=torch.float16)
+
+    for name, param in engine.module.named_parameters():
+        expected = torch.float32 if name.endswith("wo.weight") else torch.float16
+        assert param.dtype == expected, name

+    def _tensors_to_keep_in_fp32(self, dtype):
+        """The fp32 copies of the tensors the model names for fp32, keyed by name.
+
+        transformers keeps the tensors a model lists in ``_keep_in_fp32_modules`` (under fp16) and
+        ``_keep_in_fp32_modules_strict`` (under fp16 and bf16) in fp32 when it loads the model, because
+        they overflow or lose precision in half precision (T5's ``wo`` projection, MoE routing biases).
+        Casting the whole module to ``dtype`` would undo that, so they are restored after the cast.
+        """
+        pattern = keep_in_fp32_pattern(self.module, KEEP_IN_FP32_AUTO, dtype)
+        if pattern is None:
+            return {}
+        keep = {}
+        for name, tensor in list(self.module.named_parameters()) + list(self.module.named_buffers()):
+            if tensor.is_floating_point() and pattern.search(name):
+                keep[name] = tensor.data if tensor.dtype == torch.float32 else tensor.data.float()
+        if keep:
+            log_dist(f"Keeping {len(keep)} tensors the model names for fp32 in fp32 under {dtype}", [0])
+        return keep
+
+    def _restore_fp32_tensors(self, keep):
+        if not keep:
+            return
+        for name, tensor in list(self.module.named_parameters()) + list(self.module.named_buffers()):
+            if name in keep:
+                tensor.data = keep[name]
+

+    _keep_in_fp32_modules_strict = ["router_bias"]  # fp16 and bf16, as the MoE models list their routing bias
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.wi = torch.nn.Linear(HIDDEN, HIDDEN, bias=False)
+        self.wo = torch.nn.Linear(HIDDEN, HIDDEN, bias=False)
+        self.register_buffer("router_bias", EXACT_VALUES.clone())
+        self.register_buffer("scale", torch.ones(HIDDEN))
+
+
+def _dtypes(model):
+    return {name: t.dtype for name, t in list(model.named_parameters()) + list(model.named_buffers())}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.inference
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+def test_init_inference_keeps_listed_tensors_in_fp32(dtype):
+    if dtype not in get_accelerator().supported_dtypes():
+        pytest.skip(f"{dtype} not supported by {get_accelerator().device_name()}")
+    model = ToyModel().to(get_accelerator().device_name())
+
+    engine = deepspeed.init_inference(model, dtype=dtype)
+
+    dtypes = _dtypes(engine.module)
+    assert dtypes["wi.weight"] == dtype
+    assert dtypes["scale"] == dtype
+    assert dtypes["router_bias"] == torch.float32
+    # Kept as loaded, not rounded through half precision and cast back.
+    assert torch.equal(engine.module.router_bias.cpu(), EXACT_VALUES)
+    # `_keep_in_fp32_modules` applies under fp16 only, the way transformers applies it.
+    assert dtypes["wo.weight"] == (torch.float32 if dtype == torch.float16 else dtype)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.inference
+@pytest.mark.skipif(torch.float16 not in get_accelerator().supported_dtypes(), reason="fp16 not supported")
+def test_init_inference_fp16_keeps_t5_wo_in_fp32():
+    from transformers import T5Config, T5ForConditionalGeneration
+
+    config = T5Config(vocab_size=64,
+                      d_model=32,
+                      d_kv=8,
+                      d_ff=64,
+                      num_layers=1,
+                      num_decoder_layers=1,
+                      num_heads=2,
+                      decoder_start_token_id=0)
+    model = T5ForConditionalGeneration(config).to(get_accelerator().device_name())
+
+    engine = deepspeed.init_inference(model, dtype=torch.float16)
+
+    for name, param in engine.module.named_parameters():
+        expected = torch.float32 if name.endswith("wo.weight") else torch.float16
+        assert param.dtype == expected, name
